about.title: Banning Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Banning sits along the I-10 corridor in Riverside County, where traffic moves between the Coachella Valley and the Inland Empire around the clock. Recent public records show 104 injury collisions and 148 injured people in a single year here, with Friday evenings between 6 and 8 p.m. seeing a noticeable rise in reported crashes on stretches like I-10 Eastbound, I-10 Westbound, and W Ramsey Street. After a collision, decisions made in the first days often matter: photos fade from memory, vehicles get repaired or scrapped, and insurance adjusters start building their side of the story fast. LawProactive doesn't practice law or charge you anything — we simply connect injured Banning residents with an independent personal injury attorney who can review the details, deal with insurers, and help protect your right to recover. There's no obligation to move forward, and no upfront cost either way.

whyChoose.title: What to Know Before You Talk to Insurance

items.title: California's Clock Is Running
items.desc: You generally have two years from the crash date to file a car accident claim in California, but that window can shrink to as little as six months if a government vehicle or road defect was involved. Waiting to get advice can quietly cost you options.

items.title: Comparative Fault Won't Shut You Out
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, meaning you can still recover damages even if you were partly responsible for the crash. An attorney can help make sure fault percentages assigned by insurers reflect what actually happened.

items.title: Recorded Statements Can Wait
items.desc: The other driver's insurer may ask for a recorded statement soon after the accident — you're not required to give one right away. Speaking with an attorney first helps protect what you say from being used to minimize your claim later.

items.question: How long do I have to file a claim after a car accident in Banning?
items.answer: Under California law, you generally have two years from the date of the crash to file a personal injury lawsuit. If a government entity, like Caltrans or the City of Banning, may be responsible, that deadline can be as short as six months, so it's worth getting guidance early.

items.question: Why do so many crashes happen along I-10 near Banning?
items.answer: I-10 carries heavy through-traffic connecting the Coachella Valley to the Inland Empire, and public crash records show collisions clustering on both the eastbound and westbound stretches, along with W Ramsey Street. We're not labeling any road as dangerous — we're simply noting where reported collisions tend to occur, often around Friday evening rush hours.

items.question: What if the insurance company says I was partly at fault?
items.answer: California's pure comparative fault rule means you can still recover compensation even if you share some blame, though your recovery may be reduced by your percentage of fault. An independent attorney can push back if an insurer tries to inflate your share unfairly.

items.question: Does LawProactive charge anything to connect me with an attorney?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is a free service, and the independent attorneys in our network work on contingency, meaning they only get paid if you recover compensation. There's no upfront cost or obligation to move forward.
